_notes: Religious institutes (DESIGN.md §9.4). `lean` is an alignment tendency, not a fixed value: generation rolls around it. `works` are what the institute plausibly holds; the diocese hands out only what it has room for. Women's institutes fill the principal, the local superior, and the prioress; men's fill the theologian, the order parish's pastor, the hospital chaplain, the retreat master, the preacher, and the contemplative.

institutes.name: the Order of Preachers
institutes.blurb: White habits, a house of studies, and a rule that the truth is preached rather than administered.

habit.line: White tunic and scapular with the capuce; the black cappa over it in choir and outdoors.

institutes.name: the Society of Jesus
institutes.blurb: A university, a high school, and a provincial in another city who answers to Rome and not to the chancery.

habit.line: A black cassock or clerical dress; no habit of their own.

institutes.name: the Order of Saint Benedict
institutes.blurb: An abbey older than the diocese, an abbot who is nobody’s subordinate, and a guesthouse that is never empty.

habit.line: Black tunic and scapular, the cowl for choir.

institutes.name: the Order of Friars Minor
institutes.blurb: A friary, a soup line, and a habit the city recognises before it recognises a collar.

habit.line: The brown habit with the capuche and the white cord with three knots.

institutes.name: the Order of Friars Minor Capuchin
institutes.blurb: Beards, a door that is never locked, and the confessional line on Saturday that runs past the last pew.

habit.line: The chestnut habit with the long pointed capuche, and the cord.

institutes.name: the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer
institutes.blurb: Parish missions, a shrine with a novena, and men who preach a week at a time in other men’s churches.

habit.line: A black habit with a cincture and a rosary, near enough a cassock.

institutes.name: the Salesians of Don Bosco
institutes.blurb: A boys’ high school, a gym that is open late, and a way with the ones nobody else can hold.

habit.line: Clerical black; no habit.

institutes.name: the Congregation of the Mission
institutes.blurb: They have staffed seminaries since before the diocese existed, and they teach half the priests in it.

habit.line: A black cassock with the sash.

institutes.name: the Congregation of Holy Cross
institutes.blurb: Educators with a university behind them and an alumni network that answers the telephone.

habit.line: Clerical black; the Holy Cross habit is kept for the house.

institutes.name: the Order of Discalced Carmelites
institutes.blurb: A small house, a long silence, and the men other priests go to when the prayer has gone dry.

habit.line: The brown habit and scapular; the white mantle for choir.

institutes.name: the Order of Saint Augustine
institutes.blurb: A school, a parish held for a century, and a common life they take more seriously than the diocese expects.

habit.line: The black habit with the capuche, and the leather belt.

institutes.name: the Congregation of the Oratory
institutes.blurb: A house of secular priests without vows, a sung liturgy, and a parish young families drive past three others to reach.

habit.line: A black cassock with the Oratorian collar.

institutes.name: a priestly fraternity of the older rite
institutes.blurb: The 1962 books, a personal parish, and a chancery file thicker than the parish census.

habit.line: The cassock, always.

institutes.name: the Catholic Foreign Mission Society
institutes.blurb: Men home from thirty years abroad, with opinions about this country formed somewhere else.

habit.line: Clerical black or a shirt; the missions do not keep a habit.

institutes.name: the Sisters of Mercy
institutes.blurb: They built the hospital, and they ran it for a century before a board of trustees appeared.

habit.line: Black habit and veil with the white coif.

institutes.name: the School Sisters of Notre Dame
institutes.blurb: Teachers for a hundred and forty years, and half the grandmothers in the diocese were taught by them.

habit.line: Black habit and veil.

institutes.name: the Sisters of Saint Joseph
institutes.blurb: A congregation aging fast, holding works it can no longer staff and refusing to say so.

habit.line: Black, or a plain dress and a small veil.

institutes.name: the Dominican Sisters
institutes.blurb: Full habits, a median age under forty, and a waiting list for their school.

habit.line: White habit and scapular with the black veil.

institutes.name: the Franciscan Sisters
institutes.blurb: Nursing sisters, a clinic in the part of town nobody else serves, and a superior who does not ask permission.

habit.line: Brown habit and veil with the cord.

institutes.name: the Poor Clares
institutes.blurb: An enclosure on the edge of the city, praying for a diocese that mostly forgets they are there.

habit.line: Brown habit, black veil, the cord.

institutes.name: the Carmelite Nuns
institutes.blurb: A grille, a turn, and letters that arrive knowing more than they were told.

habit.line: Brown habit and scapular with the black veil.

institutes.name: the Missionaries of Charity
institutes.blurb: Blue and white, a house for the dying, and a rule that will not let them take the diocese’s money.

habit.line: The white sari with the blue border.

institutes.name: the Benedictine Sisters
institutes.blurb: A monastery with a school attached, a prioress elected by her sisters, and vespers anyone may attend.

habit.line: Black habit and veil.
